text: Standard Chartered strengthens support for Việt Nam's green transition at COP31

HÀ NỘI - Standard Chartered has reaffirmed its long-term commitment to supporting Việt Nam's transition to a low-carbon economy through a series of engagements at COP31, including discussions with Government leaders, a high-level climate finance event and agreements with two Vietnamese businesses.
The bank has worked alongside the Vietnamese Government since 2021, when the country pledged to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050.
Its activities at COP31 aimed to strengthen links between policy dialogue, international capital and investment opportunities for the country's green transition.

The engagements included a bilateral meeting with Deputy Prime Minister Hồ Quốc Dũng, a high-level panel discussion co-hosted with the Ministry of Agriculture and Environment, and the signing of memoranda of understanding (MoUs) with DaiDung Group and Stavian Group.
At the Việt Nam Pavilion, Standard Chartered representatives met with Dũng to discuss financing the energy transition in Việt Nam and ASEAN.

Key topics included investment opportunities arising from the ASEAN Power Grid and implementation of the Just Energy Transition Partnership (JETP), the development of Việt Nam's carbon market and its potential links with other markets across ASEAN, as well as opportunities in nature finance and the circular economy.

Standard Chartered said it could help connect Việt Nam's green investment needs with international capital by drawing on its global experience in structuring financing for renewable energy and power grid development.
The bank also highlighted its advisory capabilities and expertise in supporting Government agencies and businesses in the transition to a resilient, low-carbon economy.

On the same day, Standard Chartered Vietnam and the Department of Climate Change under the Ministry of Agriculture and Environment co-hosted a high-level side event entitled "Việt Nam: Responding to Climate Change in the New Era".
Speaking at the event, Dũng praised the bank's role in organising the initiative, which brought together policymakers and businesses to discuss practical solutions to climate change.

The panel focused on policy priorities, financing mechanisms and partnerships needed to mobilise climate finance, support the effective operation of Việt Nam's carbon market and strengthen its links with international carbon markets.
Participants also discussed financing requirements for industrial decarbonisation, resource efficiency, the circular economy and climate resilience.

In the presence of Dũng and representatives of relevant ministries and Government agencies, Standard Chartered exchanged two MoUs combining financing solutions with environmental, social and governance (ESG) advisory services.

Under the agreement with DaiDung Group, the bank will explore up to $50 million in green and/or sustainability-linked financing to support the expansion of the group's manufacturing facilities in line with international industry standards and sustainable factory criteria.
The financing will also support DaiDung Group's participation in green and sustainable projects being developed by its customers in various countries.
Standard Chartered will further explore opportunities to advise and support the group on ESG practices, emissions reduction and green transition initiatives.
Under its MoU with Stavian Group, the bank will continue its long-standing partnership with the company, focusing on advancing its sustainability goals.

Standard Chartered will support the arrangement and raising of up to US$150 million for eligible pipeline projects that meet the bank's Green and Sustainable Product Framework and relevant industry principles.
"We are committed to supporting Việt Nam's net-zero ambition and long-term sustainable growth.

By connecting international capital with local investment needs and bringing our sustainable finance expertise to clients and partners, we aim to help turn climate commitments into practical action," said Nguyễn Thuý Hạnh, General Director of Standard Chartered Vietnam.

"Our engagements at COP31 reinforce our commitment to working alongside the Government and businesses to advance the energy transition, develop carbon markets and unlock opportunities for a more resilient, lower-carbon economy," she added.
Globally, Standard Chartered aims to achieve net-zero financed emissions by 2050 and mobilise $300 billion in sustainable finance by 2030.
In Việt Nam, the bank's participation in supporting the Government's net-zero ambition at COP26 and COP28 reflects its continued commitment to the country's green transition. - VNS
